[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
Annie was born in 1848. She is the daughter of [[Glasgow-1780|James Glasgow]].

On 22nd February 1866 Annie Coulson Glasgow 18, of Belfast, father James Glasgow D.D. Presbyterian Minister, married William Crawford, merchant of Paris, father Alexander Crawford, Presbyterian Minister, at Fisherwick Place Presbyterian Church. The witnesses were John J. H. Gardner, and Mary Elizabeth Glasgow. <ref>Belfast SR District  https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/images/marriage_returns/marriages_1866/11518/8236119.pdf </ref> <ref> "Ireland Civil Registration, 1845-1913", , FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QGVD-C53Q : Mon Mar 04 17:18:02 UTC 2024), Entry for William Crawford and Annie Coulson Glasgow, 22 Feb 1866. </ref> 

In 1901 the Crawford family were living in Cranmore Park, William 60, born Co Antrim, York street Flax Spinning Boy Managing Director, his wife Annie Coulston 53, born India, and their son Alexander Robert 32, Clergyman, and grandchildren Lawrence C. Brown 6 born Co Tyrone, Oliver N. 4 born Co Tyrone, and a niece Mary F. Acheson 20, born Co Armagh together with 4 servants. <ref> https://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1901/Antrim/Windsor_Ward/Cranmore_Park/975291/ </ref>
A marriage for Annie Glasgow and Crawford was registered on 22 February 1866 in the Belfast district.<ref>[https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/marriage GRONI civil marriage index], 22 February 1866, Belfast district, M/1866/B1/509/2/113.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
A possible identification concerns Unnamed Glasgow daughter, Surat, 1848 (Annie candidate). At Surat, East Indies, the wife of Rev. James Glasgow, Presbyterian Church in Ireland missionary, gave birth to a daughter on 22 February, reported on 11 April 1848. The child and mother are unnamed. Annie Coulson [[Glasgow-2901|Glasgow]], whose birth is placed in India in 1848, is a possible identification of the daughter.<ref>Belfast News-Letter, 11 April 1848, p.2, Surat birth on 22 February; [https://www.newspapers.com/image/390546223/ record].</ref> 1848 is inferred from the contemporary notice’s February date. Neither child nor mother is named. The notice cannot alone make Annie’s exact birth date/place certain or establish Mary Wightman’s motherhood of another child. Her existing father/mother connections are not changed. The identification remains uncertain.
